text.text: Move each role through the pipeline, record every interview, and keep a next step on every live application.
Pipeline
Follow-ups due
Interviews
Contacts
Numbers help you steer: how many applications turn into screens, and which source works best. Keep the sheet current and look at it weekly.
Applied but quiet
What to look for
Applied for more than a week with no reply: send a polite follow-up.
Many applications from one source but no screens: change the resume or the source.
Interviews without offers: ask for feedback and rehearse the story outline.
Before every interview, run this list.
Each interview row opens with a prep checklist. This page holds the longer advice behind it.
Re-read the job posting and note three keywords
Pick two stories that show impact
Prepare three questions for the interviewer
Test audio, video and the meeting link
Send a thank-you note afterward
Story outline
Questions worth asking
What does success look like in the first ninety days?
How does the team handle disagreement?
What is the hardest part of this role?
After a rejection
Log the reason if you were told one, thank the interviewer, and move the row to Rejected. Patterns show up after five or six.
